The final change touches only three runtime files:

- `js/c-runtime/adapter-factories.js`: declared HACK/TERMCAP record fields use
  ordinary prototype accessors; a fallback proxy retains numeric pointer indexing
  and strict unknown-field errors. Inline aggregate arrays may opt into indexed
  properties and retain address projections; scalar/pointer loads remain fresh.
- `js/c-runtime/records.js`: explicit non-enumerable indexed accessors for fixed
  inline storage bypass numeric-index proxy dispatch. Unusual indices, pointer
  arithmetic and checked bounds use the existing semantics. Indices become own
  non-enumerable properties on private transport objects; reflected-property
  equivalence is not claimed.
- `js/nethack/bindings/termcap.js`: only the fixed NOMUX screen grid opts in;
  measured scalar read/write methods are selected once per cell record type,
  while every access refreshes the current memory view. Original capture policy,
  live characters/colors/attributes, aggregate copying,
  heap growth and dynamic providers remain required equivalence obligations.
No translated policy, C source, asset, compiler option, frozen dependency,
scoring rule or deadline is changed.

Utility byte-operation cleanup (2026-11-12, this workspace):
`js/ported-utilities/sfctool-runtime.js` copies the four fixed-size procedure
record arrays directly in the current Module heap;
`js/ported-utilities/tile2bmp/runtime.mjs` copies the configured bitmap header
record directly; `js/ported-utilities/sfctool-helpers.js` clears/fills valid
ranges directly. No upstream C/header, source-shaped utility policy, allocator,
compiler flag, default, recorder or game adapter changes. These are new adapter
changes, not inherited contest patches. Purpose: remove C crossings for pure
byte operations. Copy fast paths require in-bounds non-overlapping ranges;
other cases retain the original C call. Clearing requires an in-bounds range
and a numeric fill value; byte conversion remains low eight bits. Every call
reads the current heap, including after growth. Return contracts remain true
for procedure setters, Number for the bitmap memcpy wrapper, and BigInt for
utility_memset. No allocation or string/locale behavior is replaced.

## Pure-JS fixture migration (completed, 2026-11-12)

`scripts/pure-js-fixtures/` lowers isolated C **test setup and ABI helpers**
into plain JavaScript. It never compiles a NetHack game translation unit for
that implementation. Compiler dependency files are audited to reject included
upstream/prepared game C bodies; source/header/library hashes pin generated
fixtures. This uses the pinned wasm64 compiler and wasm2js offline, without
loading a Wasm engine at test execution. Original scenarios and assertions
remain in their existing `test-tu-*` files. Generated fixtures and receipts live
under `.cache/pure-js-fixtures/`. All138 registered subsystem tests now use
pure JS with Wasm denied, and all138 pass against original C. The validation
receipt records the full cohort plus successful targeted reruns for five repaired
suites and retains the failed attempts. The44 recorder sessions were not run by
this migration. BOTL uses the explicitly recorded --jitless test profile.

Additional migration repairs (2026-11-12, validation ongoing): generated
fixtures now include explicitly declared JS drawing/glyph/NHLUA dependencies,
connect existing Unix and SDK filesystem services, decode C `open` varargs,
and route policy frees through fixture ownership observers when present.
MAIL preserves the original controlled UID/passwd/stat/reader callbacks.
INVENT selects the current `.cache/tu-probes` original-C build by default;
its older author-cache reference has a zero object catalogue (dagger subtype
and merge fields are0), unlike current original C and JS (both1). Explicit
custom reference directories remain supported.
SFSTRUCT selects the isolated original-C SDK reference because its assertions
compare exact private descriptor numbers; host descriptors cannot supply that
contract. No serialization assertions are removed.

Lua C API checks use the existing auxiliary diagnostic formatter, retaining
argument numbers, function names and source prefixes. Bytecode nil-call errors
now retain the calling instruction's name/location through traceback handling.
Lua integer arguments keep all64bits across fixture imports. `lua_setallocf`,
`lua_tocfunction` and `luaL_testudata` connect actual allocator/function/userdata
state. `io` uses real JS stdio streams and file userdata;10 original-C cases
cover standard-stream types, temporary-file bytes/positions, line iteration,
EOF, close, buffering and errors. Package loading and process I/O are not
certified; `popen` rejects explicitly. This is not full Lua I/O qualification.
The CVFS facade adds callback character devices, real byte delivery, EOF,
read/write errors and non-seekability; callback devices cannot be snapshotted.
Reference RPC carries device callbacks and nested reentry; queued byte writes
flush before C observations. No reference data enters implementation services.

Expected-failure assertions suspend aggregate failure recovery inside their
callbacks, preserving actual negative-control exceptions. MKMAZE gives both
engines the same scalar equal to a reference address, preserving its pointer
normalization witness across different allocation layouts. The generated
selection corpus now also uses the Wasm-denied implementation.

Standalone `setenv`/`unsetenv` use the same instance-owned input map as `getenv`.
Formatting accepts exact unsigned64 capacities without allocating their full
size, preserving the pinned regular `vsnprintf` implementation (distinct from
SDK integer-only optimized variants). RUMORS initializes its line buffer before
an ignored EOF read: this hardens the original undefined empty-file path,
retains successful file reads, and matches observed original-C empty-file
results. Recorder equivalence of this hardening is untested.

The runner binds game calls to existing JS library adapters and production
ported policies, and libc/storage to standalone JS services. It preserves
MEMORY64 scalar/callback transport, real stack frames, live memory views and
stdio streams. Missing imports throw. Fixture growth allocation expressions
are adapted to actual 16MiB heap growth with a small owned allocation, retaining
buffer-replacement/reentry checks and avoiding geometric test-only exhaustion.
Original native-reference fixtures retain their original allocation requests.
Assertion recovery uses the compiler's setjmp transformation and JS longjmp
transport; it must not suppress unrelated exceptions.

Where a native original-C runner is unavailable, `reference.mjs` runs the
existing original-C reference build in a **separate process** through binary
observation RPC. That reference process may use Wasm. Wasm/network globals
remain denied in the process executing the JS implementation; no reference
memory or helper is shared with it. This extends reference availability without
claiming native-host equivalence for those remaining reference builds.
Validation is ongoing; no recorder or scoring run is authorized by this task.

The entry points for all138 registered TU suites now select JS-only fixtures;
this records migration wiring, not a passing aggregate. The82 newer entry-point
edits retain their assertion-site counts (`.cache/pure-js-fixtures/test-adaptation.json`).
PAGER supplies a valid PM_HUMAN species for its monster-disguise cases instead
of an object-type number outside mons. DUNGEON pointer observations prefer live
allocation ownership over old freed ranges, retain the most recent freed range
for opaque dangling-pointer identity after teardown, and never dereference it; all live bytes, allocation lifetime
metadata, unknown pointer bytes and scalar witnesses remain compared.
MONMOVE initializes the corpse inventory case with PM_HUMAN instead of
NON_PM (-1), avoiding the original unchecked `mons[-1]` access, and adds a
PM_LEPRECHAUN corpse comparison for the permissive branch. Assertions remain.
CFGFILES corrects four direct OPTIONS helper inputs to include the delimiter
required by the original helper; it retains all four values and comparisons.
END retains its original SDK reference/fixture profile: the composed native
signal-header profile has a token/function-table collision and is not used to
assert END signal equivalence. Reference labels now distinguish native host C
from original C in an isolated process. `npm test` / `test:pure-js` build the JS
fixtures and run only subsystem tests. They do not invoke recorder/scoring.

Shared C runtime additions are real anonymous stdio temporary files (linked
briefly with exclusive creation, unlinked while open, closed normally), pinned
musl/WASI C-locale strerror messages, bounded case-insensitive byte comparison,
and an explicit signed scanf saturation option for native-C comparisons. The
SDK scanf profile remains the default. C binding construction accepts an optional
injected DataView provider; its ordinary JS-owned-memory path is unchanged. Six
reference observation contexts use that provider instead of heap copying.

The Lua ABI adds actual C-function identity recovery and allocator replacement,
including updating the managed allocation tracker and using the current allocator
for later calls. Unregistered ABI function addresses fail explicitly. Lua fixture
setup opens the existing base/coroutine/table/string/math/utf8/os/debug providers;
it does not replace or claim complete luaL_openlibs/package/io support. Original
NetHack Lua policy entry points and their assertions remain under test.

Compiler intermediates are discarded after successful fixture builds. Runtime
uses only hashed JavaScript and ABI JSON. The original-C reference channel
preserves typed byte arrays, errno, output callbacks and independent instances;
reference instances are retired when their exported observations are no longer
reachable. This fixes observation transport differences rather than normalizing
policy output. Full aggregate validation is still required before completion.

code uses an internal shadow grid. Shadow tracks characters, foreground colors,
bold/inverse/underline and DEC graphics, with no independent background field.

bold normal white from actual stdout; this was not a whitespace diagnosis.
Remaining failures need individual investigation, not blanket attribution to
shadow capture or an emulator. The user has not authorized changes to the frozen
harness; none are included here.

The user requests readable JavaScript replacements, one complete C translation
unit at a time. Function names and boundaries, comments, variable names and
control flow must stay the same except for necessary C/JS semantic differences.
ABI plumbing and test/context helpers live outside each translated TU. **No next
TU may begin until the current JS replacement links with remaining C and passes
its differential tests and public suite.** Current baseline before migration is
44/44. The first TU, ISAAC64, passed 39,830 original-C/hybrid output and state
comparisons, the actual mixed link, the integration suite, and 44/44 public

The game's import table contains `isaac64_init` and `isaac64_next_uint64`; its
actual HOBJ list excludes `wasm/isaac64.o`. All four public APIs are separately
exercised by the C-caller hybrid probe. The frozen harness remains unchanged.

| J01 | `js/ported/isaac64.js` | Translate the entire `src/isaac64.c`, preserving its eight original function boundaries (four private helpers, four public APIs), comments, variable names and loops. BigInt masks and BigUint64Array stores reproduce uint64 wrap; array fill/set replace memset/memcpy. Preprocessor/type-only syntax is not runtime JS. No constructor, ABI wrapper, algorithm split or unrelated helper is placed in the TU. The existing frozen JS ISAAC implementation is untouched. |

Preserve RNG state in original C linear-memory structs; derive layout with the same wasm64 Clang, never assume native layout. Fresh views per call survive memory growth. Keep uint64 values as BigInt, normalize signed i64 ABI parameters to unsigned, and convert pointers only at the binding boundary. This temporary bridge does not make the rest of the program pure JS. |

The first TU's scope excludes libc, Lua, ncurses and the compression library;
those remain in C/Wasm. The translation process must account for C's configured
preprocessor branch explicitly instead of silently dropping active behavior.

### Second TU: nhmd4.c (J05, validated)

`js/ported/nhmd4.js` preserves its four original function boundaries and all
original comments. C's STEP/F/G/H/SET/GET macros expand inline, with original
STEP invocations retained as comments; no extra JS helper functions split the
algorithm. Uint32 coercions and logical shifts preserve unsigned arithmetic;
typed-array set/fill and subarray preserve copies, zeroing and pointer movement.
Size arithmetic uses remainder/floor operations to avoid JS's 32-bit bitmask
truncation. The compiled Wasm branch writes `ctx.block` in SET; this scratch
state is preserved. `ctx.clear()` is an external ABI helper for the original
whole-struct final memset, including buffer/block, not a fifth TU function.

Extend J02–J04's existing registry, bindings, generated layouts and probes for
this TU. Original-C reference and mixed C→JS probes use MACOS/NOPANICTRACE just
like the game, enabling its CRASHREPORT branch. Direct MD4 vector, chunk/state,
counter-wrap, context-copy and memory-growth checks are required because the
public suite does not prove crash-report digest coverage. These passed 1,287
original-C/hybrid comparisons, including seven RFC vectors and the million-a
vector; full state is checked after every tested update and final clearing is
verified. `scripts/test-tu-structure.py` also checks the current simple TUs'
function inventory/order and preservation of every original block comment.
It is not a general C parser or a proof of control-flow equivalence. Final
audit restored ISAAC's two omitted preprocessor comments; executable JS is
unchanged. Both ports together pass 44/44 public sessions with every RNG,
screen/cursor and animation match, plus the integration suite. `wasm/nhmd4.o`
is absent from the actual HOBJ list and all three public MD4 APIs appear as
JS imports in the game Wasm. Logs: `.cache/build-wasm-nhmd4.log`,
`.cache/test-wasm-nhmd4.log`, `.cache/nhmd4-public.stderr.txt`.
At this gate, no third TU had begun. Frozen test harness and native source unchanged.
The original C may still be compiled as a generated Makefile prerequisite or
for native utilities/reference probes; neither original TU object is linked
into the Wasm game. Current validation used the prepared tree with `--resume`;
the reproducible full-build path contains the same explicit object exclusions.

### Third TU: strutil.c (J06, validated)

`js/ported/strutil.js` preserves all nine original functions, their parameters,
names and original comments. It uses byte-addressed C memory, signed char
reads and unsigned byte writes, rather than JS strings or regular expressions.
The only intended control-flow adaptation is `goto pmatch_top` becoming a
labelled infinite loop/continue because JS has no goto. C pointers are numeric
addresses and int casts use signed 32-bit coercion. The inline buffer size,
struct layout and LARGEST_INT come from the matching Clang-built C probe.

`c-runtime.js` scopes synchronous dependencies around each ABI call and restores
the preceding scope on return or exception/longjmp. This avoids sharing one
game's C memory with another game. The bindings in `wasm-runtime.js` and
`tu-library.js` access the current heap after every possible C allocation;
strbuf fields stay in the original C struct. C libc strlen/strcpy/strcat/strchr,
NetHack alloc/free and lowc remain C dependencies; MONITOR_HEAP is not enabled
in this configuration. `tu-support.c` is a narrow ABI shim for the original
variadic panic call so Clang, rather than JS, constructs its varargs. It does
not replace panic's behavior or add game logic. The build compiles and links
this shim with the same game flags. Pure JS conversion is still incomplete.

`tu-strutil-probe.c`, the extended `build-tu-probes.py`/`write-tu-layouts.mjs`,
and `test-tu-strutil.mjs` compare original C and C-caller/JS builds for buffer
content and capacity, allocation transitions, CRLF handling, byte/case-sensitive
wildcard matching, the 32767-byte length guard, independent contexts and heap
growth inside an allocation callback. 8,352 comparisons passed. Both probes
link the original C alloc.c/hacklib.c dependencies; only their isolated panic
records its formatted message and longjmps back to the test. Production still
calls NetHack's actual panic. This also verifies that the dependency scope is
restored across longjmp. The private fuzzy-skipping branch is preserved but
has no reachable caller in this configured TU; it has not been independently
exercised. The full clean game build passed, including native helpers. Its
actual link excludes `wasm/strutil.o`; its import table contains Strlen_,
strbuf_append/init/empty and pmatch/pmatchi. strbuf_reserve is called inside
the JS TU; strbuf_nl_to_crlf is not imported by this configured game. Both
are additionally exercised through C callers in the hybrid probe.

All three JS ports together pass 44/44 public sessions: 11,405/11,405
screens/cursors, 792,838/792,838 RNG calls, 1,483/1,483 animation frames and
no runtime errors. The existing integration checks and all three TU test
sets pass. Logs: `.cache/build-wasm-strutil.log`,
`.cache/test-wasm-strutil.log`, `.cache/strutil-public.stderr.txt`.
No fourth TU has begun.
No frozen harness, reference recording or pristine submodule edits are made.

### Fourth TU: rect.c (J07, validated)

`js/ported/rect.js` preserves all ten original functions, parameters, names,
comments, loops, branches and recursive calls. Its three static variables
rect/n_rects/rect_cnt become properties of a per-game R state object: separate
Wasm game instances must not share ES-module static state. `c-runtime.js`
scopes R alongside C and restores both after nested calls and exceptions.
Numeric C pointers become field views or an indexed array proxy backed by
the original C allocation. C struct assignment uses value copies, including
local snapshots during recursive splitting; aliased pointer arguments stay
aliased. All of this binding support lives in `wasm-runtime.js`, outside the
translated TU. View fields use Clang-derived offsets and coordxy width, and
reacquire memory after allocation/growth. No rectangle algorithm is in C glue.

`tu-library.js` provides ABI declarations, including the original by-value
rect_bounds arguments (Clang's wasm64 ABI passes pointers to their copies).
Wrappers snapshot those arguments. C rn2 remains the randomness provider;
its calls still flow through the original recorder/RNG path. C alloc/free
and diagnostics remain dependencies. `tu-support.c` adds two narrow wrappers
for the existing constant panic/impossible invocations, letting Clang generate
the variadic ABI. Their messages and production implementations stay intact.
The exact allocation-failure branch and all other behavior remain subject to
the validation gates; no fifth TU has begun. Frozen/reference files unchanged.

The inherited recorder rn2 macro also sets source caller metadata. The bridge
`teleport_rect_rn2` preserves this using a header generated by
`scripts/write-tu-source-metadata.py` from the prepared source's real call
location and original function name. It invokes the original C rn2 function;
the probe checks its caller annotation as well as consumption, bounds and
results. This is not a per-recording answer substitution. `build.py` and the
probe builder generate/include that header before compiling ABI support.
Local rectangle bindings preserve coordxy-width truncation as well as C
struct copies. The probe derives the width, offsets, size, COLNO and ROWNO.
Its reference includes the original C TU without edits so private static
state can be inspected. Hybrid state remains in the per-instance JS binding.
The isolated probe supplies deterministic RNG/diagnostics dependencies, while
the game keeps the real C implementations. 3,644 state/geometry/pointer/RNG
comparisons passed, including recursion, aliased by-value outputs, capacity
diagnostics, heap growth and independent instances. The mixed game link excludes
rect.o and imports init_rect/rnd_rect/rect_bounds/free_rect/get_rect/split_rects
from JS. Other public routines are exercised through the hybrid probe and/or
called internally by the JS TU. All 44 public sessions and integration checks
passed, with all 11,405 screens/cursors, 792,838 RNG calls and 1,483 animation
frames matching. Logs: `.cache/build-wasm-rect.log`,
`.cache/test-wasm-rect.log`, `.cache/rect-public.stderr.txt`.

### Fifth TU: track.c (J08, validated)

`js/ported/track.js` preserves all SIX original functions, parameters, variable
names, comments, branches and loops. (The initial planning count of seven was
incorrect.) The game configuration includes settrack/gettrack; SFCTOOL helpers
continue compiling original C. C pointer walks become indexed coord views;
returned pointers still address the original ring-buffer entries. No algorithm
helper or split function is added to the JS TU.

The static counters and 100 coords have addressable storage in a per-Wasm-module
struct declared in `tu-support.h`/`tu-support.c`. These declarations retain C
storage, not C track logic, while original C callers and serializers need their
addresses. Capacity comes from the prepared source's UTSZ declaration via the
metadata generator. Clang-derived offsets/sizes govern every field access.
`wasm-runtime.js` provides T field/coord views and current hero/equipment views;
`c-runtime.js` saves/restores T across nested scopes. Heap accesses remain fresh
after memory growth. The hero and ring objects remain original C globals.

The ABI library keeps original C distmin and Sfo/Sfi int/coord serializers.
Labels are encoded as temporary UTF-8 strings on the C stack and that stack
space is restored after the call, including exception paths. No serialization
layout is replaced by JS. Narrow C shims expose the original global addresses,
evaluate configured update_file/release_data macros, and retain the original
fixed panic invocation. No extra negative-count validation is introduced.
At the initial implementation checkpoint, differential/mixed/public gates were pending and no sixth TU had begun; the completed gate is recorded below.
Frozen harness, recordings and pristine submodule remain unchanged.

`tu-track-probe.c` includes original track.c for the reference only and inspects
both implementations' counters/all100 coordinates. It links original C distmin;
isolated serializers record ordered types/tags/bytes, and an isolated panic
captures the same message with longjmp. Production serializers and panic stay
unchanged. `test-tu-track.mjs` passed 11,835 comparisons: empty/exact/adjacent
queries, wraparound, both stealth slots, returned-pointer mutations, all tested
save/count/free flag combinations, restoration and original >100 guard, edge
coordinates, heap growth and independent game instances. The test checks scope
restoration even when panic/longjmp unwinds through the JS binding. Real
serialization format remains covered by the game regression suite, not the
probe's isolated transfer buffer. The mixed link excludes track.o and all six
original public APIs are JS imports in the game. All 44 public sessions and
the integration suite passed; all 11,405 screens/cursors, 792,838 RNG calls and
1,483 animation frames matched. Logs: `.cache/build-wasm-track.log`,
`.cache/test-wasm-track.log`, `.cache/track-public.stderr.txt`.

### Sixth TU: calendar.c (J09, validated)

`js/ported/calendar.js` preserves all eleven original function boundaries,
parameters, names and comments, with Number integer fields and BigInt for
configured 64-bit time_t/long arithmetic. C char-pointer parsing loops retain
their byte operations; temporary arrays/struct copies use C-stack storage
provided by the ABI layer and the stack is restored around the complete
outer JS entry, including nested JS calendar calls. Whole struct tm copies
preserve all fields/padding and inherited DST through C localtime/mktime.
Clang supplies struct/field layouts and scalar widths. The moon calculation
uses truncating integer division; comparisons and original zero/-1 sentinel
behavior remain intact. No JS Date replacement algorithm is introduced.

This TU ports the EFFECTIVE prepared calendar.c, not pristine-only behavior:
it retains the inherited fixed-datetime hook/recursion fix and P03's explicit
recording-epoch/DST adaptation. Registry `reference: prepared` makes its C
oracle use that exact source. Original C source is unchanged in the submodule.
The original C nh_getenv, libc time/localtime/mktime/atoi/strtoll/strlen and
formatting remain dependencies. `tu-support.c` supplies only pointer/value
ABI wrappers, the original persistent15-byte datestr storage, and a fixed
Snprintf variadic bridge preserving its original format/capacity behavior.
All new bindings live outside the translated file. At initial implementation,
the timezone/mixed/public gates were pending and no seventh TU had begun;
the completed gate is recorded below.

Formatting uses the original C nh_snprintf wrapper, not a direct JS/libc
substitution. Its original function/line metadata is generated from prepared
calendar.c alongside the rectangle metadata. C reference/hybrid probes link
original options.c (nh_getenv) and hacklib.c (nh_snprintf) implementations.
The build manifest now also records the prepared C source SHA-256 for every
ported TU, alongside its JS checksum, to distinguish pristine/effective sources.

`tu-calendar-probe.c` and `test-tu-calendar.mjs` passed 9,116 effective-C/hybrid
comparisons across America/New_York, America/Los_Angeles, UTC, Asia/Kolkata and
Europe/Berlin, with fixed winter/summer process clocks. Cases include absent,
malformed and explicit recording epochs, fixed-datetime fallback, gap/fold
dates, leap/normalized dates, pre1970 and large64-bit dates, >4-digit output
truncation, the -1 parse sentinel, static string address/reuse, C stack balance,
heap growth and independent instances. Original nh_getenv and nh_snprintf are
linked into both probes; the isolated probe panic aborts only for untested
fatal allocation failure. The game link excludes calendar.o and uses JS imports
for the active calendar APIs. All 44 public sessions and the full integration

frames match. Logs: `.cache/build-wasm-calendar.log`,
`.cache/test-wasm-calendar.log`, `.cache/calendar-public.stderr.txt`.

### Per-TU ABI library isolation (J10)

Replace the monolithic `nethack-c/wasm/tu-library.js` with
`nethack-c/wasm/tu-libraries/<tu>.js`, preserving each declaration/helper body.
Registry entries name their library. `build.py` links every registered library;
`build-tu-probes.py` links only the current probe's library. This avoids unused
references in large C dependency files pulling unrelated JS bindings/dependencies
into an isolated probe. The game implementation and translated function bodies
are unchanged by this organization. The original table's J02/J03 references to
tu-library.js describe the earlier arrangement; these per-TU libraries supersede
that file. The next TU's full regression gate will validate the reorganized link.

### Seventh TU: stairs.c (J11, validated)

`js/ported/stairs.js` retains all seventeen original functions, comments,
parameters, branches and traversal order. Node/d_level views refer to the
original C allocations and gs.stairs head slot, with Clang-derived offsets,
scalar widths and boolean signedness. View writes keep the C list mutable for
remaining callers and serializers. Local d_level values copy raw bytes on the
C stack; null pointers remain 0. Boolean logical results explicitly normalize
to0/1, while the internal int-to-boolean call in u_on_sstairs narrows using the
configured C width instead of truthiness. All bindings stay outside the TU.

The original C dungeon/movement helpers, assign_level/on_level, allocation,
eos and strsubst remain dependencies. Narrow C accessors expose the head slot,
hero Amulet bit, special-level globals and dungeon-name addresses. Variadic
format bridges call the original Sprintf formats with typed arguments; they
do not choose stair descriptions or movement outcomes. JS retains those
decisions and exact strings/ternaries from the original source. UTF-8 encoding
is only for source string literals passed through the ABI; C-owned strings
remain byte pointers. Whole-entry stack save/restore covers temporaries and
recursive C↔JS calls. The per-TU library file is stairs.js under tu-libraries.

New `tu-stairs-probe.c` and `test-tu-stairs.mjs` use controlled external dungeon
and placement fixtures for both builds, while the game keeps its real C
dependencies. They compare nodes/order/mutable pointer aliases, search variants,
noncanonical boolean values, placement callbacks and all description branches,
plus memory growth and independent instances. At initial implementation these
gates were pending and no eighth TU had begun; the completed gate follows.
Frozen/reference files remain unchanged.

The original-C/hybrid stairs differential gate passed 3,830 comparisons.
These include all seventeen APIs, noncanonical boolean narrowing, mutable

`scripts/write-tu-inventory.py` generates `TU_INVENTORY.md` from the pristine

## Baselines and what “upstream” means

- **NetHack reference:** `nethack-c/upstream/`, commit
  `16ff59115315917b93185d026aeefea06db9b0f4` (`NetHack-5.0.0_Release`).
  Its checked-out commit and files have not been changed by this work.
- **Contest repository baseline:** `asriniva/teleport-contest`, commit
  `22d0ee93b5691075e9cc5c7392442ae2aa44b21f`, as cloned. The recorder patches,
  macOS hints, frozen scorer, JS skeleton and public recordings already existed.
- **Compiled source:** `.cache/wasm64-build/tree/` is a disposable COPY of the
  NetHack reference. The build applies the six inherited recorder patches and
  the additional source replacements below. **The executable contains modified
  NetHack C code even though the reference submodule is unchanged.**
- **Implementation locations:** source replacements currently live in
  [build.py](nethack-c/wasm/build.py), rather than separate Wasm patch files.
  Added C/JS bridge code lives in [bridge.c](nethack-c/wasm/bridge.c),
  [runtime.js](nethack-c/wasm/runtime.js) and
  [wasm-adapter.js](js/wasm-adapter.js).

## Inherited contest changes to NetHack

These were supplied by the contest repository, not introduced by this work.
The patch files are the authoritative complete diffs. There are **six** patch
files; the inherited patches README's references to eight are stale.

| ID | Patch and affected source | Actual divergence and purpose |
|---|---|---|
| R01 | [001](nethack-c/patches/001-deterministic-runtime.patch): `src/calendar.c`, `src/end.c`, `src/nhlua.c`, `src/u_init.c`, `sys/unix/unixmain.c`, `src/date.c`, `include/config.h` | Read fixed date and seed from environment; avoid recursive date lookup; set character birthday from fixed time; seed Lua's separate random generator; suppress the “very tricky wizard” message; pin build-date text; enable reproducible build metadata. Changes time, seed and one gameplay message for replay determinism. The original date parser inherits today's DST flag; retired W09 inferred replay-date DST, while current P03 pins the source recording clock. |
| R02 | [002](nethack-c/patches/002-deterministic-qsort.patch): `include/extern.h`, `include/hack.h`, `src/hacklib.c` | Replace game-facing libc `qsort` calls with stable tie-breaking by original position. A behavioral change to sorting for cross-platform determinism. |
| R03 | [003](nethack-c/patches/003-rng-log-core.patch): `include/extern.h`, `include/hack.h`, `src/rnd.c`, `sys/unix/unixmain.c` | Add RNG logging, call counters/callsite macros and startup initialization. Adds instrumentation and log-file I/O. |
| R04 | [004](nethack-c/patches/004-rng-log-lua-context.patch): `src/nhlua.c` | Annotate RNG calls made from Lua with script and call-stack context. Logging context defaults on when RNG logging is enabled. |
| R05 | [005](nethack-c/patches/005-rng-display-logging.patch): `src/rnd.c` | Optional display-RNG logging to the same RNG log with `~drn2` entries. The actual patch uses `NETHACK_RNGLOG_DISP` as an enable flag, not a separate output-file path. Our adapter does not enable it. |
| R06 | [006](nethack-c/patches/006-nomux-capture.patch): `include/unixconf.h`, `include/wintty.h`, `src/end.c`, `sys/unix/unixunix.c`, `sys/share/unixtty.c`, `win/tty/termcap.c`, `win/tty/topl.c`, `win/tty/wintty.c` | Add the 80×24 shadow screen, input/animation markers, final-frame capture, raw-output and name-edit tracking. Permit pipe input under marker mode and synthesize terminal erase/kill controls. Allow disabling macOS timed delay. This changes terminal/input instrumentation and headless startup behavior. |

## Additional Wasm source replacements

Active rows correspond to explicit `replace(...)` calls in `build.py`; retired
rows preserve the removed decisions. Active replacements are
applied after R01–R06 to the disposable source tree, before Wasm compilation.

| ID | Source location | Exact change, reason and behavioral effect |
|---|---|---|
| W01 (retired by N03) | `include/unixconf.h` | Previously: define `TERMINFO` only outside Emscripten. Removes the host terminfo dependency in Wasm. |
| W02 (retired by N03) | `include/tcap.h` | Previously: outside Emscripten retain `TERMLIB`; in Emscripten enable `ANSI_DEFAULT` and `ASCIIGRAPH`. Selects a fixed ANSI terminal instead of discovering host capabilities. This is not exact terminal emulation; see K01. |
| W03 | `include/unixconf.h` | Map `tgetch` to the added `teleport_getch` under Emscripten instead of libc `getchar`. Input is consumed directly from replay keys. |
| W04 | `win/tty/termcap.c` | Declare the added `teleport_capture` callback under Emscripten. Supports W07; no independent game logic. |
| W05 (retired by N03) | `win/tty/termcap.c` | Previously: enable the existing ANSI `nh_CD = ESC[J` clear-to-end-of-screen capability, formerly commented out. Makes that ANSI path clear the shadow screen correctly. This replacement itself is not preprocessor-guarded, but occurs after the native helper build and is used for the Wasm build. |
| W06 (retired by N03) | `win/tty/termcap.c` | Previously: set `CO=80`, `LI=24` in ANSI startup. Fixes replay terminal dimensions rather than measuring a real terminal. Like W05, applied to the build copy after the native build. |
| W07 | `win/tty/termcap.c` | Under Emscripten, flush C streams and invoke `teleport_capture(screen,x,y,isAnimation)`, then return instead of emitting the recorder's stdout marker and payload. Capture boundaries remain those from R06; transport changes. |
| W08 | `sys/unix/unixmain.c` | Make `get_unix_pw()` return a virtual `root` account with uid/gid 0, home `/home/player`, shell `/bin/sh` under Emscripten. Its libc account lookups otherwise return no account. This changes identity, save-file naming and wizard authorization outcomes; normal sysconf authorization checks still run. It is not host account lookup. |
| W09 (retired by P03) | `src/calendar.c` | Previously: set `tm_isdst=-1` before `mktime` for fixed replay dates under Emscripten. Determines DST from the replay date instead of today's season. Intentionally corrects inherited recorder behavior rather than reproducing its seasonal bug. |
| W10 | `include/global.h` | Select the `MacOS` port label for `__EMSCRIPTEN__ && MACOS`, in addition to upstream's `__APPLE__` condition. Changes platform/banner/help text without defining Apple compiler macros. |
| W11 | `include/global.h` | Undefine `PANICTRACE_LIBC` and `PANICTRACE_GDB` under Emscripten. Removes native stack walkers. Keeping crash-report UI is not full native crash-report support. |
| W12 | `src/report.c` | Exclude Emscripten from the CommonCrypto-specific macOS hashing branch. Avoids Apple-only headers/libraries. |
| W13 | `src/report.c` | Include Emscripten in the existing portable MD4 hashing branch. Also selects that branch's `/proc/self/exe` executable lookup, which is unavailable in our MEMFS; executable identification is incomplete (K04). No new hash algorithm was written. |
| W14 | `src/report.c` | Skip the native backtrace block inside web-report construction for Emscripten. Native stack frames are omitted. |
| W15 | `src/calendar.c` | Under Emscripten, override the source clock used by the fixed-date parser with validated NETHACK_RECORDING_EPOCH before calling localtime. Retain the inherited DST flag; do not change the replay datetime. This is P03, replacing retired W09. |
| W16 | `src/files.c` | Under Emscripten, call the in-process .Z codec instead of fork/exec/wait. Preserve native branch, configured .Z suffix, preflight, synchronization, success unlink and failure handling. Q02. |

## Added bridge and runtime behavior

| ID | Implementation | Divergence, reason and limitation |
|---|---|---|
| A01 | `nethack-c/wasm/bridge.c` | Add compile-time assertions that pointers and `long` are 8 bytes. Reject an incompatible data model. |
| A02 | `bridge.c`: `teleport_getch` | C→JS callback consumes the next replay character. The adapter translates CR to LF, matching the recording script's pipe-input translation. |
| A03 | `bridge.c`: `teleport_capture` | C→JS callback identifies input/animation capture boundaries. Default shadow capture uses its screen and coordinates; F01 documents the missing recorder post-encoding step. Explicit Ghostty mode instead snapshots stdout-derived state (G01–G05). |
| A04 (retired by N03) | `bridge.c`: `ospeed`, `tputs` | Previously: supply baud-rate symbol 0 and a simple character-emitting `tputs`; ignore terminal padding/affected-line count. Replaces termcap-library behavior for the headless ANSI tty. |
| A05 | `bridge.c`: `port_insert_pastebuf` | Replace native `/usr/bin/pbcopy` with assignment to `Module.teleportClipboard`, trimming one final newline. **No system clipboard integration or browser UI consumer exists.** |
| A06 | `nethack-c/wasm/runtime.js` | Override Emscripten's `quit_` to throw its exit exception instead of setting the host Node process's exit status. The adapter reports nonzero game status as an error. Module exit is isolated from scorer process exit. |
| A07 | `js/wasm-adapter.js` | Instantiate a fresh module and MEMFS per segment; install the supplied rc file, seed, fixed date and environment; invoke `main` with `-u` and the rc-derived player name. The module gets replay inputs, not recorded screens/RNG answers. |
| A08 | `wasm-adapter.js`: environment | Fix game/log paths to `/nethack` and `/rng.log`; HOME/.nethackrc now come from Q03 rather than the retired /home/player default; set `USER=LOGNAME=root`, `TERM=xterm-256color`, marker/raw-key/no-delay flags, supplied seed/date, and process timezone (host-resolved timezone if absent). Date fallback is `20000110090000`; seed fallback is 0. N02 additionally sets TERMINFO=/nethack/terminfo and LINES=24/COLUMNS=80. The adapter does not change the host process's timezone or implement its own timezone database. Browser execution uses browser local time. |
| A09 | `wasm-adapter.js`: exhaustion | Stop on exhausted keys using Emscripten's `unwind` control token. This stops execution at the input boundary without native process shutdown/EOF cleanup. Return captured frames and buffered RNG log. |
| A10 | `wasm-adapter.js`: RNG output | Read the C log from MEMFS; remove numeric counters and normalize spaces around `=` for the existing scorer's expected format. Does not change random values. |
| A11 | `wasm-adapter.js`: persistence | Compare `/nethack` files to embedded baseline and serialize changed/deleted files through the frozen VFS API under `/teleport-wasm64-state.json`, using base64 for binary data. Restore changes into the next segment's fresh MEMFS. This substitutes for a persistent native filesystem. |
| A12 | `wasm-adapter.js`: persistence filter | Originally excluded bones with numeric-suffix transient files. P02 now preserves the reserved bon prefix before filtering level/lock files; cross-segment restoration is tested. Compression is now supplied by Q01/Q02. |
| A13 | `wasm-adapter.js`: capture/errors | Collect screens, cursor triples and animation groups; reject runs with no captured boundary; collect diagnostics for errors. Default capture uses R06 shadow state and visibility 1; explicit Ghostty mode uses actual stdout and cursor visibility. |

## Temporary libghostty terminal backend (development only)

Authorized as a temporary abstraction while developing the eventual plain-JS
submission. This dependency is explicitly ineligible in the final contest entry
because it is Wasm. The game, account policy, date policy and persistence filter
were not changed by this backend integration. Frozen files, scorer, recording
scripts and reference sessions were not edited.

| ID | Location | Exact change, effect and limitation |
|---|---|---|
| G01 | `nethack-c/setup-terminal.sh`, `js/vendor/libghostty/` | Download/verify the official prebuilt **libghostty-vt 1.0.0** Wasm artifact, SHA-256 `7b428fee6d0677bc81279458f8f9a3335454834123a9ff47efb3fd177f6da5a8`. Preserve its MIT license and source attribution. Source URL is recorded in the vendor README. The terminal uses a separate wasm32 module/memory; the NetHack game remains wasm64. No rebuild of Ghostty or native Ghostty app is required. |
| G02 | `js/terminal-backend.js` | Add replaceable `write(bytes)`, `writeByte(byte)`, `snapshot()` and `dispose()` interface backed by libghostty. Node loads the artifact from the repository; a browser loader exists but browser integration remains unverified. Runtime replays make no network requests in Node. Library instantiation has no Wasm imports. A pure-JS backend can replace this implementation later. |
| G03 | `wasm-adapter.js`: module `stdout` callback | Capture actual C stdout bytes through Emscripten's standard-stream byte callback, preserving escapes and partial sequences. Batch them into libghostty and flush at the existing R06/W07 boundaries. In explicit Ghostty mode, ignore shadow contents; do not feed serialized shadow frames into the emulator. |
| G04 | `terminal-backend.js`: stdout conversion | Convert stdout LF to CR+LF to reproduce a Unix tty's OPOST/ONLCR behavior. The generic `write(bytes)` entry point accepts already-terminal-encoded bytes unchanged. This is terminal-device output processing, not game logic. Initialize G1 with `ESC ) 0` (DEC line drawing), introduced for the old ANSI_DEFAULT build which omitted G1 designation. This initialization remains only in the optional Ghostty backend and is inactive in default shadow mode; the ANSI build path itself is retired by N03. |
| G05 | `terminal-backend.js`: snapshot | Use Ghostty’s own VT formatter to serialize its screen, preserving DEC/Unicode and styles without a custom cell decoder or a frozen Terminal import. Disable scrollback (option 28 = 0) so snapshots contain only the 80×24 screen. Disable formatter state extras, normalize structural CRLF to LF, convert the first 16 indexed colors to equivalent standard SGR codes for the frozen decoder, and query the actual cursor separately. No frozen files are changed. |
| G06 | `terminal-backend.js`: styles | Preserve Ghostty’s serialized foreground/background colors and attributes, including RGB. The unchanged frozen comparator interprets only its supported subset; richer output may still mismatch. Serialization uses a 256 KiB buffer and reports an error if that capacity is exceeded. |
| G07 | `wasm-adapter.js`: backend selection/lifecycle | Originally defaulted to libghostty; N04 now defaults to shadow, with `TELEPORT_TERMINAL=ghostty` as opt-in. Dispose Ghostty state/handles/allocations in `finally`, including replay failures. Expose optional terminal diagnostics separately from scored outputs. Each segment gets a fresh terminal. No fallback to shadow happens automatically after an emulator error. |
| G08 | setup/tests/docs | Originally called `setup-terminal.sh` from `setup-wasm.sh`; N01 removes that automatic dependency; ignore the downloaded terminal `.wasm` artifact in Git. Add `scripts/test-terminal.mjs` and run it only for explicit Ghostty checks after N05. Document temporary eligibility, dependency provenance, backend selection, output conversion, and snapshot limitations. |

**Capability layer after N01–N03:** real terminfo replaces the earlier ANSI
bypass. Ghostty is only an optional output emulator; neither default shadow
capture nor the optional emulator supplies a replacement capability table.

## Build, dependency and configuration differences

| ID | Location | Exact choice and effect |
|---|---|---|
| B01 | `nethack-c/setup-wasm.sh` | Add SDK setup pinned to emsdk commit `1693ce7359fc9694f198694f902a2cc061239b86`, Emscripten 4.0.10, Lua 5.4.8 with SHA-256 verification. Store dependencies in `.cache/` by default; `EMSDK` may override SDK location. Initialize the existing NetHack submodule. No global installation or shell-profile edits. |
| B02 | `nethack-c/build-wasm.sh`, `wasm/build.py` | Source SDK environment; verify NetHack commit and SDK Clang 21.0.0; create a clean disposable source copy, apply inherited patches and build native helpers/data before Wasm. Native helper compiler is host Clang 21, not the identical SDK Clang binary/revision. On macOS use installed Command Line Tools directly. Prefer GNU make. `--resume` reuses prepared source and does not reapply source replacements; use a clean build after changing those replacements. |
| B03 | `build.py`: native hints | Derive hints from inherited `nethack-c/macosx-minimal`, replacing install prefix and compiler. Use `LUA_USE_POSIX` for Lua, rather than the native recorder script's macOS `LUA_USE_MACOSX`. Pin build `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1777723200` and build-process `TZ=UTC`; these do not set replay timezone. |
| B04 | `build.py`: C compilation | Compile NetHack with `-O2 -g -I../include -DNOTPARMDECL -DNO_TIMED_DELAY -DMACOS -DNOPANICTRACE -DNO_FILE_LINKS -sMEMORY64=1`. Select macOS game features on a Wasm target, use real ncurses headers and suppress delays, use file-lock implementation without hard links. `NOPANICTRACE` is not a blanket guarantee: config can still enable crash-report/PANICTRACE UI; W11/W14 disable native walkers explicitly. `__APPLE__` and `__MACH__` are not defined by this work. |
| B05 | `build.py`: Lua/bridge | Rebuild Lua with emcc/emar/emranlib, `-O2 -sMEMORY64=1`, `LUA_USE_POSIX`; compile bridge with `-O2 -sMEMORY64=1`. Lua source is not edited by the new build. |
| B06 | `build.py`: link | Link a modular ES module for Node/web with memory64, `-O2 -g`, no automatic main invocation, runtime exit support, growing memory and 4 MiB stack. Export `FS`, `ENV`, `callMain`; include A06 as post-JS. Embed game data at `/nethack`. Link the wasm64 libtinfo.a under N01, not a host ncurses binary. |
| B07 | `build.py`: assets/sysconf | Copy native-installed game assets; omit native `nethack` and `recover` executables; explicitly copy upstream `sysconf` but comment active `GDBPATH`/`GREPPATH` lines because those native paths are unavailable. Create virtual save/home directories at runtime; Q03 sets HOME/sysconf from the recording profile. |
| B08 | `build.py`: build mechanics | Add Wasm `hacklib.a` archive rule; use separate `src/wasm/` objects; override target compiler/linker/Lua archive; force relink by removing the `Sysunix` stamp. Generate `js/wasm/nethack.mjs`, `nethack.wasm`, and `build.json` (compiler, source commit, platform, DST policy, memory64 and artifact checksum); P03 adds the recording-clock DST policy and default epoch. Generated source/objects/Makefiles are not independent hand edits. |
| B09 | `scripts/score-wasm.sh` | Select SDK Node (currently Node 24), default process `TZ` to `America/New_York` when absent/empty, preserve a nonempty override, and invoke the existing frozen runner directly. Unlike `frozen/score.sh`, this wrapper does not copy frozen fixtures onto `js/` before running. Frozen fixture files themselves were not edited. |

## Historical diagnosis of the 20 failures at the 24/44 baseline

This section preserves the read-only investigation of the N01–N05 build.
P01–P04 subsequently fix F01/F03/F05; F02/F04 remain outstanding.
At that investigation stage the score remained 24/44. No engine, frozen harness, recording script or reference
session was changed during this diagnosis. Diagnostic helpers and replay outputs
are local artifacts under `.cache/terminfo-diagnosis.json`,
`.cache/terminfo-diagnosis-lines.jsonl` and `.cache/terminfo-replays/`.
All 285 failing boundary frames were inspected; 59 are style-only and 226 have
other differences. All segment frame counts in this run match the references.

| Finding | Evidence and cause | Scope / confidence |
|---|---|---|
| F01 — missing recorder screen encoding | `scripts/record-session.mjs:43–76` compresses runs of 5+ spaces into CSI cursor-forward commands, without considering active attributes. Our shadow adapter returns the raw C serialization directly. For inverse-video spaces, the frozen decoder leaves skipped cells plain, while our literal spaces acquire inverse styling. An offline diagnostic applying exactly that existing compression rule resolves all 59 style-only failing frames (2,121 differing cells). | **Sole cause in 16 failing sessions**; also affects seed2200. Characters, cursors and RNG match in the 16. This is an omitted recording-format step in our adapter, not evidence that terminfo or the shadow grid lacks spaces. No blanket suppression of attributes is proposed or implemented. |
| F02 — unsupported external compression | `src/files.c:1667` uses fork/exec to run the compressor; the Wasm environment cannot do this. Actual screens contain `Fork to compress save/0Sneaky failed.--More--`, `bonM0.1`, or `bonD0.3`, where the recordings proceed to farewell/death screens. The extra prompt consumes replay keys and changes subsequent screen state. | Both save/restore farewell frames in seed0013; parts of seed0030 and seed5006. Confirmed by code and emitted messages; no compressor replacement implemented. |
| F03 — bones files dropped between segments | `js/wasm-adapter.js:132` excludes `/nethack/[^/]+\.\d+`, including bones names such as bonM0.1/bonD0.3. Later segments create fresh levels instead of restoring bones. The two RNG-divergent sessions first diverge immediately after getbones: recorded calls restore object IDs; actual calls generate a new level. Seed5006 also misses the expected “Get bones?” and “Unlink bones?” prompts. | seed0030 segment 9 and seed5006 segment 1. Confirmed adapter filter defect; unsupported compression also affects the preceding bones-writing segment. These are persistence/service defects, not an identified PRNG implementation bug. |
| F04 — recording environment strings/configuration | seed2200 shows `/home/player/.nethackrc` where the reference uses the long documented recording HOME path. Different wrapping changes help pagination and later key interpretation. The contact screen also gains “To contact local support, contact root or games.” Our embedded sysconf contains `WIZARDS=root games`; `src/pager.c:2727` prints that formatted list. The reference omits the line. | seed2200: 9 path/pagination-related frames, 1 contact-configuration frame and 1 F01 frame. Output differences and local code paths are confirmed; the historical reason its sysconf/contact list differed is not established. No path/configuration fix implemented. |
| F05 — fixed-date/DST behavior differs from historical recorder | seed0030 has Maganasipi versus Kopasker and Swidnica versus Raciborz. `src/shknam.c:505` derives names from the character’s birth timestamp. Our W09 sets tm_isdst=-1; the inherited recorder parser carries the current clock’s DST flag into the recorded date. Diagnostic replays with the two winter timestamps shifted one hour earlier reproduce both reference shopkeeper names and associated messages. | seed0030 segments 3/7 and later scoreboards. A one-hour timestamp difference is experimentally supported and consistent with the inherited seasonal-DST bug. The exact historical recording clock state is inferred, not directly observed. Diagnostic inputs were changed only in separate local experiments; scored inputs and engine policy were not changed. |

**Sessions whose sole failure is F01:** seed0002, seed0006, seed0012,
seed0014, seed0016, seed0106, seed0108, seed0116, seed0200, seed0360,
seed0367, seed0383, seed0399, seed0501, seed2600 and seed4500.
They account for 58 style-only frames; seed2200 contributes the 59th.

**The other four:** seed0013 (F02), seed2200 (F01/F04), seed0030
(F02/F03/F05 and resulting scoreboards), and seed5006 (F02/F03).
RNG traces match exactly in 42/44 sessions; only the two bones-related sessions
have RNG differences. No new fix, build or official score was produced by this
investigation; 24/44 was the measured result at that stage. Current Q01–Q04 result is 44/44.

## Known defects and incomplete equivalence

- **K01 — terminal equivalence:** shadow capture, real terminfo and recorder
  post-encoding now match every public screen/cursor. Exact identity to the
  historical database outside exercised capabilities is unverified. Optional
  Ghostty remains outside this claim; richer styles exceed the frozen decoder.
- **K02 — bones persistence:** P02 fixes numeric-suffix bones exclusion; Q01/Q02
  add working .Z compression. All public bones/save sequences and RNG traces
  match. Arbitrary native ABI/save-file compatibility is not fully audited.
- **K03 — compression limits:** Q01/Q02 replace the unavailable subprocess with
  format-compatible ncompress. Native bidirectional tests and public sessions
  pass; compressed byte identity is not guaranteed. .Z cannot detect all
  corruption/truncation because it has no checksum or original-length field.
- **K04 — Apple/native integration:** A05 is module-local storage only; W13's
  executable lookup is unavailable; W11/W14 omit native stack traces. Keeping
  feature menus is not evidence that all native operations work.
- **K05 — lifecycle:** A09 stops at input exhaustion without native exit
  cleanup. Combined with persistence/terminal differences, multi-segment
  output can differ in frame count and later positional comparisons.
- **K06 — browser integration:** the interactive browser UI still runs the
  original JS skeleton. Browser Wasm gameplay and clipboard integration have
  not been verified or completed.
- **K07 — timezone scope:** behavior is based on Node's supported timezone/Date
  semantics. General POSIX `TZ` compatibility and every DST ambiguity were not
  tested. P03 now reproduces the recorder parser’s inherited DST behavior from
  an explicit fixed recording clock; its default is a documented assumption.

- **K08 — submission eligibility:** the contest README's Rules explicitly
  require plain JavaScript and prohibit Wasm. The current Emscripten engine is
  a local development/comparison implementation, not an eligible submission.
  A pure-JS NetHack engine that still depends on a Wasm libghostty terminal
  would also violate that rule. A vendored pure-JS terminal library appears
  compatible with the documented runtime restrictions; the rules do not
  explicitly approve every third-party library. Preserve all frozen files.
  See [contest rules](https://github.com/davidbau/teleport-contest#rules).
  Earlier discussion established technical harness compatibility but omitted
  this explicit submission restriction; that recommendation is corrected. G01–G08
  were subsequently authorized expressly as temporary development tooling.

## Continued JS migration

### J13 — sys.c translation and configured C memory views (validated)

`js/ported/sys.js` translates the three original sys.c functions with identical boundaries and original comments. Runtime branches use Clang-derived build flags for original preprocessor alternatives. Options and crash-report globals remain C-addressable; `tu-support.c` relocates only sysopt storage and exposes addresses plus the fixed original panic diagnostic. The per-TU ABI library retains native getenv, dupstr and free. Typed views preserve int/long/pointer widths and both format arrays; the original inactive seduction setter stays inactive. C initialization pointer-orphaning and cleanup omissions are preserved, rather than silently corrected. No account, terminal, save-format or feature defaults change. The configured build is covered by original-C differential probes; other preprocessor configurations and the unreachable invalid PERS_IS_UID panic branch are not yet tested. New metadata/probe registration and generated layouts are part of this divergence. Verified: 183 original-C/hybrid comparisons; all original boundaries/comments; mixed memory64 link excludes sys.o and imports all three JS entry points; all 44 public sessions pass with 11,405 screens/cursors, 792,838 RNG calls and 1,483 animations matching. All earlier TU probes and platform/integration checks pass. Logs: `.cache/build-wasm-sys.log`, `.cache/test-wasm-sys.log`, `.cache/sys-public.stderr.txt`.

### J14 — rip.c translation and tombstone pointer/output ABI (validated)

`js/ported/rip.js` will replace exactly `center` and `genl_outrip`, retaining tombstone templates, original comments, byte centering/wrapping and output order. C char-pointer arrays and line allocations remain in Wasm memory; JavaScript pointer arithmetic uses the Clang pointer width. Native allocation/string functions, fixed-signature printf wrappers, formatkiller and window callbacks remain C dependencies. The existing ported calendar supplies yyyymmdd. JS signed-byte reads and BigInt long values preserve byte/integer behavior. The build's DUMPLOG/dedication flags determine original conditional branches; no text or defaults are intentionally changed. New standalone C/hybrid probes, layout metadata and build registration are included. Verified: 501 original-C/hybrid byte-exact tombstone/callback/allocation/stack comparisons, all original boundaries/comments, actual mixed memory64 game import with rip.o excluded, 44/44 public sessions with every screen/cursor/RNG/animation matching, and full earlier-TU/platform/integration suite. Both static templates were checked against C literals; inactive DUMPLOG/dedication runtime paths are preserved but not separately compiled/tested. Logs: `.cache/build-wasm-rip.log`, `.cache/test-wasm-rip.log`, `.cache/rip-public.stderr.txt`.

### J15 — date.c translation and shared version metadata (validated)

`js/ported/date.js` will replace the two effective date.c functions, including the inherited contest deterministic build-date patch. Initially the exported nomakedefs structure and constant initializer remained C data in the temporary ABI support file while function logic moved to JS. J22 retires that temporary initializer; only shared storage remains C. Per-game JS state retains the original populated flag. Clang-derived offsets/unsigned-long widths and compiler date/time strings preserve the current SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH build setting. Native libc time/string/allocation routines and version-description helpers remain dependencies, with only fixed-signature formatting adaptation. The original tm zero initialization (including tm_isdst=0) stays intact. The NETHACK_REAL_BUILD_DATE presence override and optional git strings retain existing behavior. Both pristine C comments and effective patched comments are preserved. Verified: 2,645 effective-C/hybrid comparisons across five process timezones, all original boundaries/comments, both JS game imports with DATE_O excluded, all 44 public sessions with every screen/cursor/RNG/animation matching, and the full prior-TU/platform/integration suite. Optional git configurations beyond current metadata are not separately compiled/tested. Logs: `.cache/build-wasm-date.log`, `.cache/test-wasm-date.log`, `.cache/date-public.stderr.txt`. Other platform configurations are not claimed tested.

J15 build detail: `wasm/build.py` filters registered ports from both HOBJ and the separate DATE_O setting. Its emitted link inventory now includes HOBJ, DATE_O and TARGET_HACKLIB, so the date exclusion is checked against the actual game inputs rather than only the ordinary object list. Native helper builds continue using their original C sources.

### J16 — alloc.c active-function translation and native allocator ABI (validated)

`js/ported/alloc.js` will replace all six functions active in the configured game: alloc, re_alloc, fmt_ptr, dupstr, FITSint_ and FITSuint_. Unsigned alignment rounding, signed/unsigned integer conversions, the four-buffer pointer-format ring, allocation failure checks and original diagnostics remain unchanged. libc malloc/realloc/string/formatting operations stay native dependencies; fixed-signature C bridges carry pointers and panic arguments. ### DEP01 — Standalone JavaScript dependency migration (in progress)

The user authorized beginning external dependency/runtime migration with
subagents on 2026-11-09. Work is isolated from the concurrently active NetHack
TU migration. The current mixed C/Wasm engine, terminal default, frozen files,
recordings and build configuration remain the active reference. New standalone
services do not establish game integration or replace the current public score.

Planned additions: `js/services/unix-compress.js` implements the pinned
ncompress-compatible Unix `.Z` byte codec; `js/services/terminfo.js` and embedded
pinned terminal data implement the terminfo interfaces used by NetHack, rather
than curses windows/rendering. New focused development tests compare each with
native dependencies. Production services must not import Node built-ins, load
Wasm, access host files, fetch data or create subprocesses. Test tools may use
native dependencies as independent oracles. `scripts/audit-js-dependencies.py`
and `dependency-inventory.json` record measured dependency sources, external
calls and a staged runtime-removal backlog. Static inventory is evidence for
scope, not proof of a complete link-time closure or standalone execution.

The purpose is to establish independently executable JavaScript services before
changing the active runtime. Compression must preserve `.Z` framing, adaptive
code widths/reset behavior and existing status/error semantics; not every
truncated or corrupt `.Z` stream is detectable. Terminfo must use the pinned
entry and preserve queried capabilities/parameter expansions, with unsupported
features disclosed. Lua, regex, remaining libc, memory/global state, persistence,
startup and capture migration are not implemented by these first services.
Validation is pending; no new equivalence claim is made at this stage.

DEP01 standalone implementation gate (2026-11-09):

- `js/services/unix-compress.js`: byte-only pure-JS translation derived from
  public-domain ncompress 5.0. `compressUnixZ`/`decompressUnixZ` accept Uint8Array
  and return status/bytes/error. Hash-table lookup becomes a Map; per-call state
  replaces process globals and byte arrays replace file descriptors. Encoding
  preserves configured 16-bit block mode and 1024-byte batching/checkpoints;
  decoding handles declared 9–16-bit and non-block streams, including the
  reference's declared-9 width behavior. Status 2 retains non-shrinking output;
  the future file adapter must apply NetHack's existing cleanup/prompt policy.
  Existing service rejection of header-only empty compressed input is retained.
  This is not a streaming API, file adapter or universal corruption detector.
  `scripts/test-js-compress.mjs` passes 364 byte comparisons against the pinned
  native codec and macOS compress/uncompress: exact configured encoder bytes,
  every width, 11 adaptive CLEAR resets, binary/tiny/empty inputs, large-input
  ratio arithmetic, non-block streams, statuses, detectable errors and recovery.
- `js/services/terminfo.js` and `terminfo-data.js`: pure-JS compiled-entry parser,
  tgetent/tgetflag/tgetnum/tgetstr, tparm/tgoto and callback tputs. The full pinned
  3,462-byte entry is embedded unchanged with SHA-256, provenance and ncurses
  permission notice; capability tables retain ncurses 6.5 ordering. Parser
  supports little-endian 16/32-bit numeric and extended entries. Original C
  pointers are represented as byte strings and explicit caller byte areas;
  terminal selection/state is instance-local. Explicit dimensions replace host
  TTY queries. Pinned-entry termcap fixups (including sgr0/alternate charset)
  are retained. Delay requests use an optional callback; baud-rate pad bytes,
  actual TTY timing, terminal discovery, legacy termcap coordinate syntax and
  general setupterm postprocessing are not implemented. Lowercase uninitialized
  tparm variables follow configured ncurses 6.5 zero initialization; host 6.0
  differs there. `scripts/test-js-terminfo.mjs` passes 3,058 comparisons with
  host ncurses using identical terminal data, plus 22 malformed-entry cases,
  modern/extended/cancelled entry checks, area writes and state isolation.
  Comparisons cover every queried capability, 256 foreground/background colors,
  all 1,920 cursor positions, RGB, 512 attribute combinations and expression/
  output behavior. Independent review also compared all 497 capability lookups
  with native ncurses and verified tables against include/Caps. Review fixed
  literal-dollar scanning, cancelled extended offset counts and escaped-percent
  parameter detection; maintained tests reproduce the fixes.
- `scripts/audit-js-dependencies.py` and `dependency-inventory.json`: reproducible
  structured inventory with source hashes/line evidence, configured/build
  snapshot distinction, Lua sandbox/API observations, libtinfo-only source
  mapping, ABI/libc/runtime candidates and ordered migration gates. `--check`
  detects snapshot drift without writing. 1,460 distinct TU dependency names
  and 105 libc/terminfo call-like names were observed at this snapshot; neither
  is a proven reachable closure. No full-ncurses UI source inventory is included.
- `scripts/test-js-dependencies.sh` runs both oracle suites and
  `scripts/test-js-dependency-isolation.mjs`. The latter executes all three
  production modules in a VM with host/package imports and dynamic imports
  rejected, WebAssembly/process/Buffer/fetch unavailable and runtime code
  generation disabled. Compression and terminal operations pass in that
  environment. The VM-module flag belongs only to the development test loader;
  production modules require no VM API or experimental flag.

All combined standalone gates pass on Node 22.23.4. Tests may compile native
oracles and use host files only in unique dependency scratch directories;
production services perform neither. Browser/Chrome execution and full-game
integration are untested. No game build/default, frozen file or recording was
changed by DEP01. Public recordings were not rerun for these inactive services;
existing mixed-engine scores are not evidence for their integration. Lua,
regex, remaining libc services, JS-owned memory/state and startup/capture/
persistence migration remain open. The next integration gate is replacing

J57 development native test portability details (native-basic-test-changes.md):

# Native basic-suite portability changes

Scope: only scripts/test-tu-sys.mjs, scripts/test-tu-alloc.mjs, scripts/test-tu-posixregex.mjs. No production code, fixture, shared backend, builder, or calendar edits. Only syntax checks were run.

## SYS

The test now reads each backend's actual config/string/field descriptors. Emscripten metadata must still equal the checked-in generated layout exactly. All shared compile constants must match; the explicitly platform-dependent PANICTRACE_LIBC flag is checked by its actual selected initialization branch. A per-backend expected value follows static zero initialization, poisoned population, configured initialization, and preservation through release/no-op calls. Every snapshot checks this field exactly before comparing the remaining fields. This preserves the native MACOS stack-walker configuration and the Emscripten explicit undefinition rather than pretending they share a configuration.

## ALLOC

All non-NULL full-width pointer strings, ring-buffer aliases, allocation, failure, and ownership checks remain exact comparisons. Only NULL %p is checked against each actual libc contract: Darwin `0x0`, Linux `(nil)`, Emscripten `0`. A new native host requires an explicit expectation rather than silently accepting arbitrary text. No pointer text is rewritten or normalized.

## POSIXREGEX

The test now reads actual metadata separately for both backends, checks the context and field containment, and retains exact generated Emscripten-layout comparison. Host regex_t layout is allowed to differ (Darwin nhregex40/err32 versus Emscripten72/err64). All original behavioral cases and comparisons remain present. Behavioral platform mismatches are intentionally not hidden: the existing fixture exposes only regex_compile/regex_match/regex_error_desc wrappers, with no independent direct-libc result API.

Completion of POSIXREGEX portability requires minimal direct-dependency probe exports (no parser or regex policy implementation):

- direct regcomp(&regex->re, pattern, REG_EXTENDED | REG_NOSUB), returning its actual status;
- direct regexec(&regex->re, text, 0, NULL, 0), returning its actual status;
- direct regerror(status, &regex->re, caller_buffer, supplied_capacity), returning its actual size.

Run those on independent real contexts so wrapper state and direct-engine state do not alias. Their outputs permit independent assertions of wrapper status/error-buffer policy for host-specific empty regex, invalid syntax, nonportable escapes, error messages, and codes. Preserve cross-backend exact assertions for portable regex semantics and preserve the complete Emscripten reference-vs-hybrid comparisons. Do not invent diagnostics or disable pattern cases to make the native suite pass.

Calendar remains unchanged; native mktime versus Emscripten Date-based mktime differences need a separately authorized dependency-level plan.

J57 test-only portability details (native-terminal-test-changes.md):

# Proposed native terminal test correction (test files only)

`test-tu-ioctl.mjs` and `test-tu-unixtty.mjs` now read the original C probe's layout separately for each actual Module. The native Darwin termios struct, flag widths, flag values, control-character indexes, baud constants and signal-handler constants remain unchanged. Game, ported algorithms, fixtures and shared backend are untouched.

IOCTL maps only the three named signal-handler identities between backends and checks the actual signal/action constants before comparing call order. Unknown handler values retain their complete unsigned 64-bit pattern. Opaque termios snapshots compare the common poisoned prefix across unequal layouts; every get/set additionally checks the entire structure within its own backend, including native-only bytes and padding. The empty windows operation preserves every raw byte. Equal-layout Emscripten references still compare the complete original snapshots.

UNIXTTY sets corresponding named flags, baud rates and control characters using each backend's real metadata. Native buffers retain poisoned opaque bytes; only the named semantic fields are translated during setup. Cross-host snapshots compare each relevant flag and each shared control-character role. Equal-layout Emscripten snapshots remain byte-exact. Independent operation checks verify whole get/copy bytes, complete tcsetattr inputs, preservation of saved structures, unrelated flag bits, unrelated control characters and padding. Optional host-only control-character branches remain active. Their exact fpathconf call counts are checked using the actual configured feature metadata before consecutive calls are grouped for shared call-order comparison; the actual `_PC_VDISABLE` and `TCSADRAIN` arguments are separately checked. No blanket snapshot or trace skip is added.

Limits: raw structures with different layouts cannot be compared byte-for-byte across platforms. Host-only optional control characters have no cross-platform counterpart; their writes are confined to their actual fields and fpathconf counts are checked. This does not test an actual terminal or deliver actual process signals: the original isolated fixtures still intercept those native operations. No new native capability or recording equivalence is claimed.

Validation so far: both test files pass JavaScript syntax checks. No unit suite or build run by the editing agent; parent owns execution and final results.

The C formatted-input rules do not define an integer conversion whose result is not representable in the destination long. The observed Darwin and Emscripten outcomes therefore are pinned-libc evidence, not a claim that undefined C conversions have portable semantics. No native result is replaced, clamped, emulated, or made to equal the other libc. Regular Emscripten-C mode keeps its existing overflow comparison path.

J57 POSIXREGEX independent dependency details:

# POSIXREGEX test-only native portability

Changed only scripts/tu-posixregex-probe.c and scripts/test-tu-posixregex.mjs. No production, shared backend, registry, builder, or coloratt changes. Node syntax check passed; no builds or test executions were run.

New probe exports for the builder:

- probe_dependency_compile(const char *pattern, struct nhregex *regex) -> int
- probe_dependency_match(const char *text, struct nhregex *regex) -> int
- probe_dependency_error(int status, struct nhregex *regex, char *buffer, size_t capacity) -> size_t

Their bodies directly call actual regcomp, regexec, and regerror with the original dependency signatures/flags. They contain no regex parser, copied wrapper policy, status translation, or diagnostic rewriting.

In native mode the suite now keeps the original Emscripten reference and JS hybrid as its first two modules, retaining every original exact status/error-buffer/lifecycle comparison. The host-native module is an additional third backend. Each host regex has a separately allocated direct-libc context with the same input pattern. Wrapper compile status and stored errors are asserted against actual independent regcomp results. For successfully compiled contexts, every applicable input is checked against actual independent regexec, including original error preservation versus REG_NOMATCH. Each host diagnostic buffer, including untouched padding, is compared to independent actual regerror output plus the original wrapper's three literal policy messages. Each buffer capacity uses that backend's compiled BUFSZ; layout/context assertions use its actual compiled metadata. No host diagnostic text or numeric error code is hardcoded.

A fixed subset of ordinary POSIX ERE patterns retains exact cross-engine compile and ASCII-match assertions. Locale-dependent non-ASCII input, nonportable escapes/invalid syntax, and empty-pattern behavior are independently checked against the actual host engine instead of claiming different engines must produce identical diagnostics or accept identical extensions. All original patterns and inputs remain in the suite. If only the host accepts a pattern, all inputs are exercised on that host too.

regex_match explicitly requires successful prior compilation. A backend which rejects a pattern is not called with an invalid compiled regex; its compile result, error buffers, retained caller buffer, and freeing are still checked. This respects the original API precondition rather than invoking undefined library behavior. Both the wrapper context and independent dependency context are freed for every iteration; a final assertion checks that no tracked host context remains. Memory-growth and independent-instance cases remain present.

This is an Emscripten-C/JS differential suite augmented with native-C/direct-dependency portability checks and cross-engine portable semantics. It does not claim that a Wasm regex_t can be reinterpreted as host regex_t, or that JavaScript is running against a host regex engine.

The development probe builder exports dependency_compile/dependency_match/dependency_error for POSIXREGEX and parse_offer/parsed_offer for MINION. These are test APIs only; no game link/import/default changes.

J57 VERSION pinned-libc witness details:

# VERSION native fallback dependency witness

Only `scripts/tu-version-probe.c` and `scripts/test-tu-version.mjs` changed. No VERSION game function, production adapter, upstream source, harness, shared tooling, or libc behavior changed.

New fixture exports:

- `char *probe_fallback_witness(size_t size)`: initializes an independent 8193-byte storage area to `0xa5`, places the existing fixture literal `5.0.7-fallback` after a one-byte prefix guard, and invokes actual `nh_snprintf("version_string", 25, out, size, "%s", out)`. It returns `out`.
- `void *probe_fallback_witness_base(void)`: exposes the guard address, permitting the unit to assert the returned interior pointer is exactly base+1.
- `size_t probe_fallback_witness_size(void)`: exposes the 8192-byte output span.

The native-only comparison adjustment is restricted to operation0 (`version_string`) when its version metadata is missing or empty. Every original size and metadata case remains. A separate actual original-C Emscripten instance retains the complete original-C/Emscripten versus JS comparison for all of those fallback cases, including full output/state/table/io/trace and stack checks. The native original function is executed separately; every native output byte must equal the independently initialized direct libc dependency witness. All other native state must equal its pre-call state, and the exact fallback/returned-pointer trace must be `mdlib:.;returned:1;`. The witness itself must return its actual base+1 pointer.

The inherited fallback passes an overlapping destination/source to formatted output. C does not define that overlap, and Darwin and Emscripten libcs produce different bytes. The inherited `nh_snprintf` also writes `str[size-1]` on the size-zero truncation path. The witness prefix guard makes the resulting pinned implementation write observable; the unit asserts its zero byte at size0 and untouched `0xa5` at all other sizes. This does not make the original source operation portable or remove its undefined behavior; it preserves existing pinned-implementation evidence without demanding that different libcs agree on undefined input.

No tests or builds run for these edits; the parent must export the three helpers and rebuild before verification.

Builder exports all three development witness getters; no production export changes.

# Proposed native calendar test bridge

Only development probe and test files change: `tu-calendar-probe.c`, `native-calendar-hybrid.mjs`, and `test-tu-calendar.mjs`. Production calendar.js, its eleven original function boundaries, the production runtime, compiler flags and frozen harness are unchanged.

The probe exports typed calls to actual native time/localtime/mktime, bounded nh_getenv, strlen/atoi/strtoll and native formatting, plus a separate zero-only 15-byte datestr buffer. These helpers contain no calendar, parsing, DST or timezone algorithm. A second independent native Module runs the existing calendar.js functions through the existing createPortedRuntime.calendar entry.
